title: Using Extraordinary Optical Transmission to Quantify Cardiac Biomarkers in Human Serum
protocol: Coat a 220 nm-thick layer of negative electron beam resist onto a 600 µm-thick 4-in silicon wafer.
Write the designed nanohole array on the wafer using an electron beam lithography system.
Set the e-beam exposure dose to 110 µC cm−2 and write at a current (I) of 800 pA.
Develop the resist by immersing the wafer in the developer solution for 10 s.
Let the wafer dry in air.
Deposit a seed layer of metal on the silicon wafer.
Electroplate the wafer in a nickel sulfamate bath for 95 min at a current density of 0.7 A dm−2.
Continue electroplating the wafer for 125 min at a current density of 12 A dm−2 to achieve a final thickness of 300 µm (20 nm).
Ensure the pH value is maintained between 3.5 - 3.8 and the temperature between 52 - 54 °C during electroplating.
Separate the nickel mold from the silicon substrate using gentle mechanical force.
Soak the nickel mold in about 100 mL of positive photoresist removal reagent overnight to remove residues.
Dry the nickel mold at 100 °C for 3 h in an oven.
Clean the nickel mold in a plasma etching system with O2 gas at 10 sccm and 100 W for 3 min.
Coat 150 µL of heptadecafluoro-1,1,2,2-tetrahydrodecyl trichlorosilane (FDTS) on the nickel mold in a self-assembly monolayer (SAM) coating machine at 80 °C.
Imprint nanopatterns on a glass wafer coated with a 300 nm-thick layer of photo-curable NIL resist using a nano-imprinter at 10 bar pressure and 40 °C for 10 min.
Transfer the mold, photoresist, and glass wafer to a UV light curing system.
Photocure with 75 mW cm-2 of UV exposure for 30 s.
Perform a blank etch of the photoresist on the glass substrate in an RIE system using O2 gas flow at 10 sccm and 50 W power for 2 s.
Deposit a 5 nm-thick layer of chromium (Cr) for metal adhesion.
Deposit a 100-nm layer of gold (Au) for plasmonic sensor on the glass wafer using an electron-beam deposition machine with Cr at 1 Å s−1 and Au at 2 Å s−1 rates.
Perform lift-off of the photoresist by O2 plasma etching for 3 min followed by a 15-s sonification step in acetone.
Dice the sample into 5 mm × 5 mm chips.

Set up apparatus to make optical measurements such that a beam of white light exiting through the end of the transmitter optical fiber is collimated and incident on the sensor surface (nanohole array) at 90°.
Collect the transmitted signal with the receiver optical fiber.
Record it with a UV-visible spectrometer operating within the range of 300 to 1,000 nm.
Set the acquisition time for each frame to 20 ms.
Average 100 frames to obtain the final spectrum to lower the noise in the measurements.
Clean the sensor chip after each measurement with a surface-active cleaning reagent and dry it with nitrogen gas.
Deposit the standard RI liquid into the liquid cell, with the RI varying from 1.31 to 1.39.
Immerse the sensor chip in the standard RI liquid and align it with the beam of white light.
Obtain the transmission spectrum.
Clean the sensor chips by sequential immersion in isopropanol, acetone, and deionized water.
Dry at room temperature in a stream of dry nitrogen gas.
Incubate the sensor chips in an ethanolic solution of 0.4 mM 10-carboxy-1-decanethiol and 1.6 mM 1-octanethiol for 12 h at room temperature.
Rinse thoroughly with ethanol and dry at room temperature.
Mix 75 mM sulfo-N-hydroxysuccinimide (sulfo-NHS) and 15 mM 1-ethyl-3-(3-dimethylaminopropyl) carbodiimide (EDC).
Immerse the chips in this mixture for 15 min.
Spot 50 µL of 200 µg/mL anti-troponin antibody solution made in pH 4.5 acetate buffer on the sensor surface.
Incubate for 30 min.
Immerse the sensor chip in 1 M ethanolamine-HCl solution to deactivate unreacted esters.
Rinse the chip with deionized water and dry it in a stream of dry nitrogen gas at room temperature.
Spot 100 µL of 1% bovine serum albumin (BSA) solution onto the surface to block non-specific binding.
Incubate for 15 min.
Rinse the sensor chips three times in phosphate-buffered saline (PBS) solution.
Insert the chip into the measurement cell to record the transmission spectrum.
Spot 50 µL of cTnI standard onto the chip surface and incubate in a moist environment for 30 min.
Rinse the sensor chips three times in PBS solution and insert it into the measurement cell to record the transmission spectrum.
Submerge the chips in 50 mM glycine-HCl (pH 2) for 1 min and then rinse in PBS solution three times to regenerate the chip surface.
Measure the transmission spectrum in PBS to verify the success of the regeneration step.
Run the multiplexed SPR sensor chip on the SPR system with PBS-T buffer.
Activate 3 out of the 6 available channels with a mixture of EDC (0.2 M) and sulfo-NHS (0.05 M) for 5 min.
Perform a 5-min injection of 50 µg/mL antibody 560.
Perform a 5-min injection of 1 M ethanolamine-HCl solution.
Rotate the sensor chip by 90°.
Inject cTnI standards at different concentrations (75, 30, 7.5, and 2.5 ng/mL).
Observe conjugation to the antibody at spots of interaction on the chip in real time through SPR readout.
Regenerate the chip by injecting 50 mM glycine-HCl (pH 2) for 1 min.
